findings.message: Instance fix. This round changed only the tool description (mcp-utilisation.ts:10) and the README, and now both document the defect. `people` is still built only from `mine.status` and `teamWeek` rows, and both need a `time.week` row. Anyone who logged nothing that week is left out, including the viewer. `below` therefore can never return the person who is furthest below target. The description tells chat to answer 'either has no timesheet or isn't someone you may see', which still merges 'logged nothing' with 'not visible'. Fix: list every person the viewer may see (the same 071 scope `teamWeek`/`hoursVisibleTo` applies, over hr people). Show anyone without a week at 0 h with status null, against their target, with every working day before today in `missingDays`.
findings.scenario: Maya manages Dinesh. Dinesh logs nothing in 2026-W43. `get_week_utilisation {week:'2026-W43', below:80}` omits Dinesh, who is at 0%, and lists only people who logged some hours.

findings.message: Still open. Whether Leave is present is decided by `to_regclass('leave.request')`, not by whether the module is installed. The new `leaveVisible` flag (line 63) and the leave adjustment both hang off that check. The new no-Leave test only covers a database where Leave was never migrated. It doesn't cover the real case: Leave switched off with `AMAX_MODULES_DISABLED=leave` on a database that already has its tables. Fix: gate `leaveIn` and the `leaveVisibleTo` check on the installed-module registry, not on the table existing, and test with Leave's tables present but the module disabled.
findings.scenario: Leave is installed, then switched off with AMAX_MODULES_DISABLED=leave. Its tables remain, so `get_week_utilisation` still subtracts old approved leave from targets and marks people `leaveVisible: false`, even though Leave is off.

findings.message: The fix removes 'no status = draft' only when Time answers. If Time can't be asked (`installed(tx,'time.week')` is false), `fromTime` is an empty Map. If Time no longer has the week id (purged or erased week), the id is missing from the result. In both cases `counts` returns false and the hours are dropped exactly as a draft would be, with nothing on the row or the team figure to say so. 'Could not ask' still reads as 'not counted'. Fix: when a row has a `week_id` and neither the local copy nor Time gives a status, flag that person's figure as incomplete/unknown (as Reports does with 'Leave not visible'). Don't silently exclude the row.
findings.scenario: Time is disabled (no time.week table), and logged_hours rows carry a week_id with no week_status row. Utilisation drops those hours and shows a lower billable % with no mark. The same happens for a week_id whose time.week row was purged.

findings.message: The variant test has two cases, and the second does not drive the real path: it plants the missing-status state with a hand `delete from reports.week_status`. The previous finding named an Admin's locked log into an old approved week, and that variant is still missing. The test also has no case for Time not answering (no status from either source). Fix: add the locked-log variant, and a case where the status is missing because the event wasn't consumed (for example, emit the approval with the Reports handler absent), not deleted by hand.
findings.scenario: Remove the `weekStatuses` fallback for one path (for example, only call it for submitted weeks). Both existing cases can stay green while an approved week touched by a locked log drops its hours.

findings.message: `weekStatuses` is a cross-module contract read that takes no reader and applies no data scope. It returns the timesheet status of any week id in the tenant. The architecture says contract reads apply the caller's data scope (see the earlier `weekTotals` lesson). Fix: take a reader (a viewer, or a `contextFor.job` system context) and filter to the weeks that reader may see, or document why status-by-id is exempt.

The README says 'Migration 0004 backfills every week that existed when 072 shipped from Time, so a week with no status is a new draft'. No migration 0004 exists, and the code now looks the status up through Time's `weekStatuses` instead of treating it as a draft. Fix: describe the contract lookup.
